clue.text: Preserving expert's hard evidence

parts.note: smoking fish or meat over a fire is a way of curing and preserving it
a gun is an expert or champion, as in a top gun; the 's stands for 'is' joining the pieces

explanation.surface: A conservation specialist's work is presented as solid proof of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserving' reads as an adjective on the expert, but it is the curing sense, giving SMOKING.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for incontrovertible proof of guilt, from a pistol still smoking after being fired.

clue.text: Considerable problem discussed

indicators.note: discussed means talked about, so the word for problem is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set in school

explanation.surface: A sizeable difficulty is being talked over.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal usage, as in 'that was some storm', where the word means remarkable or considerable.

clue.text: Reason pen's useless making pig cry

parts.note: the reason a pen is useless is that it holds nil ink; nil is the letter O
a pen's contents are its ink

explanation.surface: Someone explains why a writing pen won't work, and it somehow produces a farmyard noise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Reason pen's useless' as a riddle: the reason is 'O INK', that is, no ink at all. The blog treats it as a cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The grunting noise a pig makes, written as an imitative word.

clue.text: Put away cider near cat going wild

indicators.note: going wild means running out of control, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stores away cider next to a cat that is getting agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away someone, colloquially, is to lock them in prison.

clue.text: Copper overseas turned up a haul

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to haul is to drag something heavy

explanation.surface: A policeman abroad finds a big catch has appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is slang for a police officer; 'overseas' points to Ireland, whose police force is the Garda Síochána.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish term for a police officer or the Irish police force, a foreign cop to British solvers.

clue.text: Iffy going round city centre of Cardiff without protection

indicators.note: going round means surrounding, so the word for iffy encloses the next piece

parts.note: iffy means doubtful or unsure
EC is the postcode for the City of London

indicators.note: centre of picks out the middle letter of the seven-letter Cardiff

explanation.surface: Someone uncertain about a route circling the middle of Cardiff, feeling exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any security or guarantee, as with a loan that has no collateral behind it.

clue.text: Bathe disheartened tramp

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, so the middle letter of the word for bathe goes

parts.note: to steep something is to soak or bathe it in liquid

explanation.surface: A dejected vagrant takes a wash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tramp' looks like a vagrant noun, but it is the verb meaning walk heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: Both verbs describe walking or treading, a tramp being a heavy plodding stride.

clue.text: They annoy and upset rubbish teachers

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down entry the word for rubbish is read upwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense or rubbish
mentors are trusted advisers or teachers

explanation.surface: Bad teachers both irritate and distress their pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun for people who pester or torment, matching the plural pronoun subject.

clue.text: Uninspired novel read in Sept

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A dull book was what someone read in September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' sits as a noun beside 'Uninspired', but it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dull, prosaic and lacking imagination.

clue.text: Film about an independent dog beautician

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for film wraps the following pieces

parts.note: a mist is a thin film of moisture
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A film is made about a freelance beautician who looks after dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty specialist who cares for the hands and nails.

clue.text: Prompt for start of debate

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: start of takes the opening letter of debate

explanation.surface: A cue that gets a discussion going.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt is to nudge or poke someone into action.

clue.text: Working out and working out, neglecting runs after poor races

indicators.note: after places the trimmed exercise word behind the shuffled races
poor means badly made, so these letters are reshaped
neglecting means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: working out at the gym is training
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A sprinter, after disappointing races, works out by training without running.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase appears twice: first as the definition (figuring out), then as the gym sense in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: finding out or determining something for certain.

clue.text: Media people ordered best cars to cover route

indicators.note: to cover means to wrap around, so the shuffled letters enclose the next piece
ordered means put into a new sequence, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a road is a route

explanation.surface: Journalists have the finest cars arranged to cover a route, like a motoring feature.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio and television presenters work in the media.

clue.text: Unannounced reviews of location Europeans reported

parts.note: a spot is a place or location

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word for these Europeans is given by its sound

parts.note: Czechs are people from the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: Surprise inspections of a place where Europeans have been reported.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspections made at random without warning, to catch things as they really are.

clue.text: Using intelligence from faith teaching, bishop in church meeting

indicators.note: in places the first pair of pieces inside the church-meeting pair

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a rally is a mass meeting
RE is religious education, faith teaching in British schools
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clever bishop draws on religious education at a church gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a school subject in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb for acting by thought and intellect rather than emotion.

clue.text: Pressure on fragile candidate

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
re means about, on the subject of
tender means delicate or fragile

explanation.surface: A delicate candidate buckles under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant to a throne or title, who stands as a candidate for it.

clue.text: Tots gathering at one end of house play up

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so the word for tots holds the next pieces

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, as is a dram
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of house

explanation.surface: Toddlers gathering at one end of the house start misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tots' and 'play up' suggest toddlers being naughty; tots are drinks and 'play up' means exaggerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to exaggerate or make something seem more striking than it is.

clue.text: Lodge in middle of America unopened

indicators.note: unopened means losing the opening letter

parts.note: center is middle in American spelling

explanation.surface: A lodge sits in the heart of the US, still shut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of America' looks like the middle letter of America; it means the US spelling of a word for middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge a complaint or appeal is to submit or record it formally.

clue.text: Greek character half-cut with another

indicators.note: half-cut means half the word is cut away, so only the second half of with survives

parts.note: another Greek character, eta

explanation.surface: A Greek man who is drunk sits with another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk; here it trims the word 'with' to its back half.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: One perusing books and article about Italy's theatres

indicators.note: about here means going round to the other side, so the article lands after the letter for Italy

parts.note: an auditor examines a company's account books
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An accountant and a piece about Italian playhouses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article about Italy' puts A round to the far side of I, giving IA rather than AI; I is the international vehicle code for Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of the Latin word for the hall where an audience sits, hence theatres.

clue.text: Ability to ride's hard with leaderless Viking boat

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: leaderless means the first letter is lost

parts.note: a Norseman is a Viking
a ship is a boat

explanation.surface: Riding is hard, and a Viking without a chief in a longboat would know.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill in handling and riding horses.

clue.text: Maybe sportsman's captain not very quiet

indicators.note: not means without, so the following letters are removed

parts.note: a skipper is a captain of a team or ship
pp is the music notation pianissimo, very quiet

explanation.surface: A sporting captain is anything but softly spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on the slopes is an example of a sportsman, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: One place to study temperature

parts.note: uni is short for university

explanation.surface: A single place to study temperature, like a weather station.
explanation.definitionFit: A single whole item counted as one.

clue.text: Lost claret in part of Wimbledon

indicators.note: in part of means the answer sits within a stretch of the word Wimbledon

explanation.surface: Someone spilled their wine during part of the Wimbledon tennis fortnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claret' is a red wine, and old boxing slang for blood.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing blood, with claret as slang for blood, is to have bled.

clue.text: Chilly swimmer crossing lake

indicators.note: crossing means stretching across, so the fish word goes round the next letter

parts.note: a cod is a fish, a swimmer
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A fish swimming across a lake feels the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: low in temperature.

clue.text: Phone to receive idea of part of company

indicators.note: to receive means to take in, so the phone word holds the next piece

parts.note: to dial is to phone
a vision is an idea or concept

explanation.surface: Someone rings head office to receive a new idea for a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective for relating to a division, a section of a business.

clue.text: Oddly shady use for reports

indicators.note: oddly means taking the odd-numbered letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: Reports that are dodgy are put to dubious ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To report something is to state it; both mean to tell.

clue.text: Isolated drunk staggered around Spain

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the next piece
drunk means reeling about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A drunk staggered around Spain, alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: separated or kept apart from others.
